dedupe_keys.name: form eia 411 coordinated bulk power supply and demand program report peak load capacity resources and planned transmission by nerc area

description: Form EIA-411, the Coordinated Bulk Power Supply and Demand Program Report, collects electric reliability information from US power system planners about the supply needed to serve current and future demand. Contents: historical and projected peak load, monthly peak hour demand for the winter and summer seasons, net energy for load, net internal demand and planned (net) capacity resources, plus projections of planned high-voltage transmission line additions. Producer: EIA; the data are aggregated by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation from its regional entities. Coverage: the United States portion of the NERC regions (10 regions before 2005, 8 from 2005), shown from 2011 by reliability assessment areas such as FRCC, NPCC, MISO-US, PJM, SERC, SPP, ERCOT and WECC. Format and access: Excel workbooks on the EIA-411 page; the files listed on 29 September 2026 were the 2016 set (net energy for load, peak load, monthly peaks, summer and winter capacity, transmission lines) with an archive page. Licence: public domain; EIA's copyright and reuse page says U.S. government publications are not subject to copyright and asks users to acknowledge the source with its publication date. Caveats: regional boundaries changed over time, so series are not fully comparable; the published files end with the 2016 release; security and incident data are collected separately on Form OE-417. Simulation uses: regional demand and reserve margin inputs for resource adequacy studies and planned transmission additions for grid expansion models. Related records: data-doe-oe-417-electric-disturbance-events, data-eia-930-hourly-electric-grid-monitor and data-eia-860-annual-electric-generator-report.
